newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks end lower in volatile trading.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks end lower in volatile trading.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks closed moderately lower Tuesday after scrambling back from steep losses as investors cashed in some profits from the market's recent run into record territory.
The 30-stock Dow Jones industrial average fell 19.38 points to 6,528.41, one day after climbing through 6,500 for the first time and setting its 11th record in the last 12 sessions.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances 1,351 to 1,134 on heavy volume of 527 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index eked out a gain of 0.83 point to close at a record 1,281.20.

The market was taken on a roller coaster ride from the opening, as waves of computer programme trades sent the Dow spiralling higher, but then at its peak, knocked a full 70 points off the index, triggering New York Stock Exchange curbs as the losses exceeded 50 points.
"You've got to expect a little bit more of a roller coaster and a dicier tape with the market this extended," said Gregory Nie, technical analyst at Everen Securities in Chicago.
He said the bullish trend still seemed to be in place.
"There are a lot of sceptics still out there, and maybe they had some influence on tape action today," he said. "But I would hesitate to call this a reversal, the charts look good."
Gary Anderson of Anderson & Loe Inc., which advises money managers, said the blue-chip stocks were hit by profit-taking.
"The market zigs and zags some, but we are in a powerful uptrend," he said. "This bull market has gored a lot of pundits who thought it was dead and went bearish. It ain't dead yet."

Some of the weakness in the Dow stemmed from a drop in the shares of Caterpillar Inc., which sank 2-1/4 to 77-7/8 after investors reacted with disappointment to Deere & Co.'s earnings for the latest quarter.
Deere, which reported record earnings that nonetheless fell short of some expectations, fell 2-3/8 to 44.
Walt Disney Co., another compoent of the Dow, surged 2-3/4 to 76-1/4 after it posted robust quarterly profits due to record attendance at its theme parks and strong box office returns.
International Business Machines Corp. closed up 1/8 at 158 after rising to a 52-week high of 160-3/4 on news that it would buyback up to $3.5 billion of its common stock.
Retailer Linens 'n Things Inc. was one of the most active NYSE stocks with almost 6 million shares changing hands in its Wall Street debut. The shares closed up 1/8 to 15-5/8.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks was off 1.07 points at 755.96. The American Stock Exchange index was off 1.05 to 588.33.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks dipped 0.88 to 397.98. The average share was down 9 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,273.063 down 6.339 or 0.09 percent.
